rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiable: "docs/ is authoritative, not descriptive… When code and a doc disagree, one of them is a bug; fix both in the same commit"; gpui-components rule 13 / checklist 25 (a §6 catalog entry per component state)
summary: The §6 `TerminalTabStrip` entry documents an API signature the code does not have (`agent_status(StatusKind)` vs `agent_status(TerminalAgentState)`), omits the `attention` and `kind` builders entirely, and states a dot rule the code deliberately contradicts.
evidence:
docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:972-974 documents:
```
**API.** `TerminalTabStrip::new([TerminalTab::new(1, "nvim").activity(bool).starting(bool)
.keep_alive(Icon).agent_status(StatusKind).unread(bool).exited(impl Into<Option<i32>>)]).id(ElementId).active(usize).show_plus(bool)
```
The code takes a different type, at crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/terminal_tab_strip.rs:153:
```rust
pub fn agent_status(mut self, status: TerminalAgentState) -> Self {
```
and carries two builders the doc never names — `attention` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:126) and `kind` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:112). `grep -n "attention\|TerminalTabKind" docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` returns nothing. The doc's dot rule at :986-989 says "the active tab and an exited tab draw neither", but terminal_tab_strip.rs:177-184 returns amber for an active tab whose `attention` is set:
```rust
if self.attention { return Some(Tone::Warning); }
if is_active { return None; }
```
failure_scenario: A reader following §6 writes `TerminalTab::new(1, "cc").agent_status(StatusKind::AgentWorking)`; it does not compile, because the kit's type is `TerminalAgentState`. A reader trusting :989 reasons that the currently open tab never shows a dot and builds a "you have unread work" indicator elsewhere, duplicating the amber dot the strip already draws for `attention`. Both `attention` and `TerminalTabKind::Native` — a shipped glyph in the tab body (terminal_tab_strip.rs:374-380) — are invisible to anyone reading the authoritative catalog.
proposed_fix: In one commit: correct the API line to `agent_status(TerminalAgentState)`, add `.attention(bool)` and `.kind(TerminalTabKind)` to the API line, add `attention (amber dot that survives selection)` and `native (kind glyph before the name)` to the **States.** line, and rewrite the `unread` vs `activity` usage rule so it says the active tab draws no dot *unless* it is blocked on the reader — which is what `dot_tone` implements and what the module doc at terminal_tab_strip.rs:170-176 already explains.
verify_reason: All three claims check out. docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:972-974 writes `agent_status(StatusKind)`; the kit signature is `pub fn agent_status(mut self, status: TerminalAgentState)` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:153) — `StatusKind` is only reachable through the private `TerminalAgentState::status_kind` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:46-51), so the documented call does not compile. `attention` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:126) and `kind` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:112) are live builders — `kind(Native)` draws a GitBranch glyph before the name (terminal_tab_strip.rs:377-382) and `attention` drives the dot — and `grep -n 'attention(\|TerminalTabKind' docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` returns nothing. The dot rule at :986-989 ("the active tab and an exited tab draw neither") is contradicted by `dot_tone`, which returns `Some(Tone::Warning)` for `attention` before the `is_active` early return (terminal_tab_strip.rs:177-184) — and the code's own doc comment at :170-176 states the corrected rule explicitly, so the code is right and the doc is the bug.
blast_radius: docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:971-989 only, plus a new test module in crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/terminal_tab_strip.rs if the include_str! guard is added. Ships in the same commit as finding 3's gallery panels (same component, and CLAUDE.md requires doc+code together).
corrected_fix: The proposed fix is correct as written. One addition: `TerminalTabKind` and `TerminalAgentState` are kit-public types the §6 entry never names, so the entry should also list `TerminalTabKind::{Pty, Native}` and `TerminalAgentState::{Working, Finished}` rather than only the builder names, otherwise a reader still cannot write the call. The include_str! doc test is workable (path `../../../../docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` from src/components/ resolves to the repo root) but it asserts on prose formatting and will break on any harmless rewording — prefer asserting only on the type names (`TerminalAgentState`, `TerminalTabKind`), not on `.attention(bool)` punctuation.

rule: gpui-components rule 13 / checklist 24: "a panel in the matching examples/gallery_*.rs showing every state"; DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:1251 "If a state is not in a gallery, it is not implemented"
summary: Four shipped `TerminalTab` visual states — `attention`, `unread`, `agent_status` (working and finished) and `kind(TerminalTabKind::Native)` — appear in no gallery panel, including the one whose label claims to show "every mark".
evidence:
gallery_terminal.rs:408-423 is the exhaustive panel and covers only keep_alive, activity, exited and long names:
```rust
LAYOUT.labeled(
    "every mark",
    &t,
    TerminalTabStrip::new([
        TerminalTab::new(1, "nvim").keep_alive(Icon::FilePen),
        TerminalTab::new(2, "cc").activity(true).keep_alive(Icon::Bot),
        TerminalTab::new(3, "server").keep_alive(Icon::Server),
        TerminalTab::new(4, "test").exited(1),
        TerminalTab::new(5, "build").exited(None),
        TerminalTab::new(6, "a-very-long-terminal-name").activity(true),
    ])
```
`grep -rn "attention(\|unread(\|agent_status(\|TerminalTabKind" crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/` returns nothing, while all four are live builders (terminal_tab_strip.rs:112, 126, 133, 153) rendered by `tab_body` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:374-380, 404-409) and by `dot_tone` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:177-190).
failure_scenario: Someone changes the neutral `unread` dot to the same amber as `attention`, or changes the `Native` kind glyph, or swaps `StatusGlyph` sizes for `agent_status`. `cargo run -p fleet-ui-kit --example kit_gallery` — the repo's stated acceptance gate (DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:1253-1254) — renders identically before and after, in both themes, so the regression ships. The distinction the strip exists to draw (amber = blocked on you, neutral = wrote while you were away, per NATIVE-AGENTS.md §3.3) has no visual reference anywhere in the repo.
proposed_fix: Extend the `every mark` panel in `examples/gallery_terminal.rs` (and mirror it in `examples/kit_gallery.rs:948-957`) with tabs covering `.attention(true)` on both the active and an inactive tab, `.unread(true)`, `.agent_status(TerminalAgentState::Working)`, `.agent_status(TerminalAgentState::Finished)` and `.kind(TerminalTabKind::Native)` — the attention-on-active case in particular, since it is the only state whose rule differs from every other mark.
test_plan: `cargo check -p fleet-ui-kit --examples` proves the panel compiles; the failing-before check is a grep-style assertion in the gallery support module or a `#[test]` in gallery_terminal.rs asserting the panel builder produces a strip containing a tab with `attention`, one with `unread`, one with each `TerminalAgentState` and one `Native` tab. Before the fix no such tab exists in any example, so the assertion fails.
verify_reason: `grep -rn 'attention(\|unread(\|agent_status(\|TerminalTabKind\|TerminalAgentState' crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/` returns zero hits. gallery_terminal.rs:408-423 ("every mark") covers keep_alive/activity/exited/long-name only, and kit_gallery.rs:947-957 is the same set plus `starting`. All four unshown states render real pixels: `kind(Native)` a GitBranch glyph (terminal_tab_strip.rs:377-382), `agent_status` a StatusGlyph (:404-409), `attention`/`unread` distinct dot tones (:177-190). DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:1249-1254 states the rule as a hard one ("showing **every** state… If a state is not in a gallery, it is not implemented") and names `cargo run --example kit_gallery` as the acceptance gate, so this is a violation of an authoritative repo rule, not a matter of taste. The attention-on-active case is the one that matters most, since it is the only mark whose rule differs from the others.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/gallery_terminal.rs:408-423 and crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/kit_gallery.rs:947-957. `TerminalAgentState` and `TerminalTabKind` must be re-exported from the kit root for the examples to name them — verify components/mod.rs exports both. No src/ behaviour changes; pairs with finding 2's doc commit.
corrected_fix: Add the panels as proposed, but drop the proposed `#[test]` in gallery_terminal.rs: `#[test]` functions inside `examples/*.rs` are compiled but not run by `cargo test` (example targets default to `test = false` for harness collection), so that assertion would never fail in CI. The enforceable guard is either `cargo check -p fleet-ui-kit --examples` (already the stated gate) or a test in src/ that greps the example source via include_str!, in the style of the keymap doc test. Also mirror the new tabs into kit_gallery.rs:947-957, not only gallery_terminal.rs, since kit_gallery is the combined overview the acceptance gate actually opens.

rule: gpui-components rule 13 / checklist 24; DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:1251-1252 "If a state is not in a gallery, it is not implemented"
summary: Two production-used visual variants have no gallery panel: `Cycler::off_grid(true)` (both arrows stay live for a persisted value outside the configured steps) and `SegmentedTabs::underlined(false)` (selected background instead of the accent underline).
evidence:
The cycler panel at gallery_input.rs:725-749 shows only focused / `has_prev(false)` / `disabled(true)`:
```rust
Cycler::labeled("host", host).label_width(px(140.0)).focused(true) …
Cycler::labeled("on switch", "sleep").label_width(px(140.0)).has_prev(false),
Cycler::labeled("theme", "system").label_width(px(140.0)).disabled(true),
```
and the tabs panels at gallery_input.rs:836-850 use the default underline only. `grep -rho "off_grid(\|underlined(" crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/` returns nothing, yet both ship: `off_grid` changes arrow availability and `is_visible` (cycler.rs:88-97) and is set by crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/settings/view.rs:147 and crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/board_settings/view.rs:89; `underlined(false)` is used by crates/fleet-app/src/screens/hub.rs:443 and is documented at docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:824.
failure_scenario: A change to `Cycler::render`'s `arrow(self.off_grid || self.has_prev, ..)` predicate — or to the `!self.is_visible() && self.label.is_none()` early return — silently breaks the off-grid rendering: a persisted host that is no longer configured would render with both arrows dead, stranding the user on a value they cannot cycle away from. The gallery, the stated acceptance gate, shows no difference. Likewise a regression in the `underlined(false)` branch is invisible until someone opens the Hub.
proposed_fix: Add one labelled strip to each panel: `Cycler::labeled("host", "devbox (removed)").off_grid(true).has_prev(false).has_next(false)` beside the existing cyclers, and a `SegmentedTabs::new([..]).underlined(false)` strip beside the `tabs (h / l)` panel, then add a **States.** line to the `Cycler` §6 entry (docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:797-804), which currently has none.
test_plan: After adding the panels, `cargo check -p fleet-ui-kit --examples` must pass; the failing-before check is a `#[test]` in gallery_input.rs asserting the cycler panel's builder set contains one entry with `off_grid` true and the tabs panel set contains one with `underlined` false. Neither exists today, so both assertions fail.
verify_reason: Verified both halves. `grep -rn 'off_grid(\|underlined(' crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/` returns nothing; the cycler panel (gallery_input.rs:725-749) shows focused / has_prev(false) / disabled only, and both tabs panels (gallery_input.rs:836-850) use the default underline. Both variants are live and production-used: `off_grid` flips both `is_visible` and the arrow predicate (cycler.rs:98, 152-154) and is set at dialogs/settings/view.rs:147 and dialogs/board_settings/view.rs:89,320; `underlined(false)` changes the selected treatment (segmented_tabs.rs:160, 195) and is set at screens/hub.rs:443 and documented at docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:824. Same authoritative rule as finding 3 (DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:1249-1254). The finding's incidental claim that the Cycler §6 entry has no **States.** line is also correct (docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:797-804 has Purpose/API/Keyboard/Usage rule only), though `off_grid(bool)` is already on its API line at :800.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/gallery_input.rs:725-749 and :836-850, mirrored in crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/kit_gallery.rs, plus the Cycler entry at docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:797-804 if the States line is added.
corrected_fix: Panels as proposed. Same test-plan correction as finding 3: a `#[test]` inside examples/gallery_input.rs will not be executed by `cargo test`, so it cannot be the failing-before check — use `cargo check -p fleet-ui-kit --examples` plus, if a guard is wanted, an include_str! grep test living in src/. Note the off_grid strip should be `Cycler::labeled(..).off_grid(true).has_prev(false).has_next(false)` so it demonstrates the one thing off_grid changes (both arrows live with neither neighbour present); anything else renders identically to the existing rows and proves nothing.

rule: gpui-components rule 9 / checklist 10: named slots are the container contract — a slot the caller filled must render or the builder must not accept it
summary: `KeyValueList::trailing` is silently discarded when no `title` is set: the trailing element is only ever consumed inside `title.map(..)`, so `KeyValueList::new().trailing(stamp)` renders nothing at all.
failure_scenario: A detail-panel block built with the untitled constructor — the form three of the four production call sites already use (crates/fleet-app/src/views/detail/repo.rs:40, detail/pull_request.rs:87, dialogs/settings/view.rs:187) — adds `.trailing(FreshnessStamp::new("inspected", age))` to satisfy the §2.6 rule that every job-derived block carries an age. The stamp compiles, is boxed, and never appears: the block renders as if the facts had no age, which is the exact state DESIGN-SYSTEM §2.6 says must not exist ("A fact without an age is not a fact").
proposed_fix: Render the header whenever either half is present — `.children((title.is_some() || trailing.is_some()).then(|| { let mut header = SectionHeader::new(title.unwrap_or_default()); … }))` — or, if a trailing element genuinely has no home without a title, move the parameter onto the constructor (`KeyValueList::titled(title).trailing(..)`) so an untitled list cannot accept one at all.
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` in key_value_list.rs that renders `KeyValueList::new().trailing(Text::hint("checked 3s ago")).row("path", FactValue::text("/x"))` in a test window and asserts the produced tree contains the trailing text (via a probe element that flips an `Rc<Cell<bool>>` in its own render, which is enough to prove it was laid out). It fails today because the slot is dropped before the tree is built.
verify_reason: The code does exactly what the finding says: `trailing` is moved into the closure passed to `title.map(..)` (key_value_list.rs:88-104), so with `title == None` the `Option<AnyElement>` is dropped and nothing renders. Reproducible in two lines against the public builder — `KeyValueList::new()` (:25) and `trailing` (:47) are both public and unconstrained. The mitigating facts are real but do not refute it: no production call site currently does this (all four `KeyValueList` sites are either `titled(..)` or never call `trailing` — views/detail/repo.rs:40,111, views/detail/pull_request.rs:87, dialogs/settings/view.rs:187, views/detail/worktree.rs:163-164), and the doc comment says "on the section header", which hints at the coupling without enforcing it. So the defect is latent API, not a live rendering bug — severity low is right, and the failure scenario as written is hypothetical, not observed.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/key_value_list.rs only for option (a) — no current caller passes `trailing` to an untitled list, so nothing in fleet-app breaks; if the builder is moved to a `titled`-returning type, check crates/fleet-app/src/views/detail/worktree.rs:163-164 (the only `KeyValueList::titled(..).trailing(..)` site) and crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/gallery_data.rs:503-516, kit_gallery.rs:462. Option (b) additionally touches docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md §6 and a gallery panel.
corrected_fix: Prefer the type-level option the finding lists second, not the first. Rendering a header whenever either half is present with `title.unwrap_or_default()` produces a 20 px `section_header_h` row containing an empty `Text::label` and a right-aligned stamp (section_header.rs:30-41) — a floating stamp above an unlabelled block, which is a layout the design system has no entry for. Either (a) move `trailing` off `KeyValueList` and onto the `titled` path so an untitled list cannot accept one (a compile error is the correct failure for a slot with no home), or (b) if an untitled block genuinely needs an age stamp, give it its own right-aligned row and add that state to the §6 KeyValueList entry and a gallery panel — do not silently reuse SectionHeader with a blank label.

rule: gpui-components rule 12 / checklist 22: "a gpui::Role with no accessible name is worse than no role"
summary: `control::on_activate` stamps `gpui::Role::Button` on every element it makes clickable without ever setting an accessible name, so the whole terminal tab strip and the new-tab affordance enter the accessibility tree as anonymous buttons.
evidence:
control.rs:27-35:
```rust
pub(super) fn on_activate<E: InteractiveElement + StatefulInteractiveElement + Styled>(
    element: E,
    activate: impl Fn(&mut Window, &mut App) + 'static,
) -> E {
    element
        .role(gpui::Role::Button)
        .cursor_pointer()
        .on_click(move |_, window, cx| activate(window, cx))
}
```
Its two call sites are the per-tab hit target and the `+` tab (terminal_tab_strip.rs:344-346 `super::control::on_activate(el, move |window, cx| select(pos, window, cx))` and terminal_tab_strip.rs:445 `super::control::on_activate(el, on_new)`). Nothing anywhere in the kit sets an accessible name: `grep -rn "aria\|accessible\|\.name(" crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/` finds none.
failure_scenario: A screen reader walking the workspace announces six or seven unlabeled "button" nodes for the tab strip plus one for `+`, with no way to tell `nvim` from `cc` from `lg` — strictly worse than the untagged `div`s the same tabs would be without `.role(..)`, because the role promises a name the tree does not carry. The `gpui-components` skill lists this file and line as the existing offender and asks that it be given a name when the file is touched.
proposed_fix: Widen the helper to `on_activate(element, name: impl Into<SharedString>, activate: ..)` and set the accessible name alongside the role, then pass the tab's `name` (terminal_tab_strip.rs, where `tab.name` is already in scope at the `tab_element` call) and a literal such as `"new terminal"` for the `+` tab. If the pinned gpui tag exposes no name setter for the role, drop `.role(Role::Button)` rather than keep an unnamed one.
test_plan: Add a `#[test]` in control.rs asserting the helper's signature requires a name (`let _: fn(Div, SharedString, _) -> Div = on_activate;` style compile assertion), plus a `#[gpui::test]` in terminal_tab_strip.rs that builds the strip and asserts each tab element carries a non-empty accessible name. Both fail today: the current helper takes no name and none is ever set.
verify_reason: control.rs:31-34 sets `.role(gpui::Role::Button)` and nothing in the kit ever sets a name — `grep -rn 'aria' crates/fleet-ui-kit/src` finds zero hits. The pinned gpui does expose the setter (`fn aria_label(mut self, label: impl Into<SharedString>)`, ~/.cargo/git/checkouts/zed-a70e2ad075855582/bebe92f/crates/gpui/src/elements/div.rs:1276, alongside aria_description/aria_keyshortcuts), so the fix is available and the finding's "if the tag exposes no name setter, drop the role" escape hatch is moot. Two corrections to the finding's own facts: there are three call sites, not two — terminal_tab_strip.rs:346 (per-tab), :442 (the `+` tab) and sticky_error_slot.rs:110 — and this is a known, already-catalogued item, not a new discovery: gpui-components checklist 22 and SKILL.md:102-103 name `control.rs:32` as "the existing offender" and ask that it be named when the file is touched. It is a real accessibility defect by the repo's own rule; it is not a regression this diff introduced.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/control.rs:27-34 (signature), and all three call sites: terminal_tab_strip.rs:344-346, :440-442, sticky_error_slot.rs:109-111. `control` is `pub(super)` so the change stays inside crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components — no fleet-app churn. Existing terminal_tab_strip tests (crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/terminal_tab_strip.rs:~580+) do not assert on roles and should be unaffected.
corrected_fix: Widen the helper to take a name and call `.aria_label(name)` beside `.role(Role::Button)`. Pass `tab.name` at terminal_tab_strip.rs:346, a literal such as "new terminal" at :442, and the error text (or "dismiss error") at sticky_error_slot.rs:110 — the finding omits that third site, and leaving it unnamed reproduces the exact defect it is fixing. Drop the proposed compile-assertion test: `on_activate` is generic over `E` and takes `impl Fn`, so `let _: fn(Div, SharedString, _) -> Div = on_activate;` does not compile as a coercion of a generic fn item and proves nothing. If a test is wanted, assert on rendered accessibility state in a `#[gpui::test]`, or simply rely on the signature change forcing every call site to supply a name.

rule: docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:172-173 (§2.5 Radii): "Toasts, sheets and the scroll pill are `md`" — the doc is authoritative for `fleet-ui-kit` (docs/README.md:9)
summary: `Sheet` is the only one of the three surfaces §2.5 assigns `radii.md` that applies no corner radius at all, so the design doc and the crate disagree about the sheet's corners.
evidence:
crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/sheet.rs:92-104 — the sheet card carries bg, border and shadow but no `.rounded(..)`:
```rust
div()
    .flex()
    .flex_col()
    .h_full()
    .w(width)
    .bg(theme.colors.elevated)
    .border_l(theme.metrics.hairline)
    .border_color(theme.colors.border_strong)
    .shadow(theme.sheet_shadow())
    .overflow_hidden()
    .occlude()
```
The two siblings the same doc sentence names do apply it: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/toast_stack.rs:250 `.rounded(theme.radii.md)` and crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/scroll_pill.rs:85 `.rounded(theme.radii.md)`. A repo-wide `radii.` scan shows no `radii.md` in sheet.rs and no consumer at all for `radii.none`.
failure_scenario: A reader implementing a new docked panel follows §2.5, gives it `radii.md`, and it does not match the Jobs sheet beside it; conversely anyone editing `Sheet` to match the doc changes the shipped appearance without knowing whether the square edge was deliberate (a right-docked sheet is flush to the window edge, which is a plausible reason for `rounded_l` only). One of the two halves of the contract is wrong and neither says which.
proposed_fix: Decide and land both halves in one commit: either add `.rounded_l(theme.radii.md)` to sheet.rs:93 (flush right edge, rounded leading corners) plus a gallery panel, or amend docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:172-173 to read "Toasts and the scroll pill are `md`; the docked `Sheet` is square because it is flush to the window edge."
test_plan: Add `#[test] fn sheet_matches_the_documented_radius()` in `crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/sheet.rs` asserting the built surface's `corner_radii` equal `theme.radii.md` on the leading corners. It fails today (all zero) and passes after the `rounded_l` change; if the doc is the half being fixed instead, the test is replaced by the doc edit and the gallery panel.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/sheet.rs:92-104 carries bg/border_l/shadow and `grep -n rounded sheet.rs` returns nothing, while the two surfaces the same doc sentence names do apply it (toast_stack.rs:250, scroll_pill.rs:83). docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:172-173 says 'Toasts, sheets and the scroll pill are `md`'. Doc and crate genuinely disagree; the doc is authoritative for fleet-ui-kit, so one half is a bug.
blast_radius: docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md only. The proposed test asserting the built surface's `corner_radii` is not writable — `Sheet` is a `RenderOnce` returning an opaque `impl IntoElement` with no style accessor — so drop it; if the code half were chosen instead, sheet.rs plus the gallery sheet panel in crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/kit_gallery.rs would move.
corrected_fix: Fix the doc, not the code. sheet.rs:91-96 renders inside `deferred(div().absolute().inset_0().flex().justify_end())` with `.h_full()` and a `border_l` only — the sheet is deliberately flush to the window's right edge, which is why it has no radius and no right/top/bottom border. Amend docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:172-173 to 'Toasts and the scroll pill are `md`; the docked `Sheet` is square because it is flush to the window edge.' Adding `.rounded_l(theme.radii.md)` changes shipped appearance for a doc sentence and should not be the default resolution.
